claims.source: Swe1WEE1 can also be stabilised upon DNA damage (Palou et al., 2015) and in response to certain types of stress (Chauhan et al., 2015; George et al., 2007; King et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claims.claim: Swe1WEE1 physically interacts with histone H2B and promotes its phosphorylation.
claims.source: Interestingly, Swe1WEE1 was quite recently shown to be able to physically interact with histone H2B and promote its phosphorylation. This phosphorylation is conserved from yeasts to humans and seems to play an important role in the repression of histone transcription at the end of S-phase (Mahajan et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claims.claim: H2B phosphorylation by Swe1WEE1 is conserved from yeasts to humans.
claims.source: Interestingly, Swe1WEE1 was quite recently shown to be able to physically interact with histone H2B and promote its phosphorylation. This phosphorylation is conserved from yeasts to humans and seems to play an important role in the repression of histone transcription at the end of S-phase (Mahajan et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claims.claim: Deletion of the NEG regulatory site in the HTA1-HTB1 cluster interferes with normal repression of histones H2A and H2B by the HIR complex.
claims.source: Deletion of the NEG regulatory site (∆NEG) in the HTA1-HTB1 cluster interferes with the normal repression of histones H2A and H2B by the HIR complex and leads to their persistent transcription beyond S-phase (Figure 1a) (Eriksson et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claims.claim: Transformation of rad53K227A or tom1∆ cells with CEN-HTA1-HTB1∆NEG generates a large number of small colonies with severe growth defects and a small population of large colonies that grow almost like wild-type cells.
claims.source: When transformed in rad53K227A or tom1∆ cells, this construct generated a large number of small colonies that experienced severe growth defects and a small population of large colonies able to grow almost like wild-type cells (Figure 1b) (between 2–4 × 10−2, raw numbers are in the additional source data file for Figure 1b) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b and Figure 1—figure supplement 1a.

claims.claim: Large colonies from rad53K227A or tom1∆ cells transformed with CEN-HTA1-HTB1∆NEG have experienced a WGD and became diploid.
claims.source: FACS analysis of these two populations revealed that large colonies had experienced a WGD and became diploid (Figure 1b)
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 1b.

claims.claim: WGDs from histone overexpression were not observed in wild-type cells transformed with CEN-HTA1-HTB1∆NEG.
claims.source: This effect was not observed in wild-type cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b)
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b.

claims.claim: WGDs induced by histone overexpression are not specific for histones H2A and H2B.
claims.source: This effect was not observed in wild-type cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b) and was not specific for the overexpression of histones H2A and H2B (Figure 1c).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1c demonstrating that overexpression of H3/H4 also induces WGDs.

claims.claim: Diploids arising from histone overexpression are able to tolerate better high levels of histones than haploids.
claims.source: Growth analysis of small (n) and big colonies (2 n) in the rad53K227A mutant confirmed that diploids are able to tolerate better high levels of histones (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by growth analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1c.

claims.claim: Wild-type cells transformed with a high-copy vector containing HTA1-HTB1∆NEG (2µ∆NEG) give rise to a significant number of cells (around 1 × 10−2) that have experienced a WGD.
claims.source: Cells transformed with a high-copy vector that contains the HTA1-HTB1∆NEG construct (2µ∆NEG) vector gave rise to a significant number of cells (around 1 × 10−2, source data file for Figure 1b) that have experienced a WGD (Figure 1d).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 1d.

claims.claim: The 2µ∆NEG construct increases histone H2B mRNA by 50%.
claims.source: This construct increases by 50% the amount of histone H2B mRNA but does not induce a detectable change in the amounts of total histone H2B protein (Figure 1e and f).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by Q-PCR data shown in Figure 1e.

claims.claim: The 2µ∆NEG construct does not induce a detectable change in the amounts of total histone H2B protein.
claims.source: This construct increases by 50% the amount of histone H2B mRNA but does not induce a detectable change in the amounts of total histone H2B protein (Figure 1e and f).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1f.

claims.claim: Diploids arising from 2µ∆NEG transformation were perfectly viable and did not show any major chromosome reorganization compared to haploid or diploid strains obtained by cross.
claims.source: Diploids were perfectly viable, did not show any major chromosome reorganisation when compared to a haploid or diploid strain obtained by cross (Figure 1g)
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by karyotype analysis shown in Figure 1g.

claims.claim: Diploids arising from 2µ∆NEG transformation were able to form triploids when crossed with a strain from the opposite mating type.
claims.source: Diploids were perfectly viable, did not show any major chromosome reorganisation when compared to a haploid or diploid strain obtained by cross (Figure 1g) and were able to form triploids when crossed with a strain from the opposite mating type (Figure 1—figure supplement 1e).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1e.

claims.claim: Diploids arising from 2µ∆NEG transformation still had a small growth advantage when compared to haploids in wild-type conditions.
claims.source: Diploids still had a small growth advantage when compared to haploids in wild-type conditions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1f).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by growth data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1f.

claims.claim: WGDs were never detected in wild-type cells transformed with an empty vector (more than 2.2 × 10² colonies analysed by FACS).
claims.source: WGDs were never detected in wild-type cells transformed with an empty vector (more than 2.2 × 102 colonies analysed by FACS).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by experimental data from FACS analysis of control cells.

claims.claim: Most haploid cells transformed with 2µ∆NEG turn into a diploid state in 48–96 hr after inoculation in liquid from a petri dish plate.
claims.source: Time course experiments with these cells revealed that most of them usually turned into a diploid state in 48–96 hr after inoculation in liquid from a petri dish plate (colonies have already grown for 5 days in the plate) (Figure 2a).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by time course FACS data shown in Figure 2a.

claims.claim: Cells transformed with 2µ∆NEG show a large population of non-dividing cells and a significant decrease in the number of cells that have started to separate their chromosomes.
claims.source: Cell cycle distribution of these haploids transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector in a strain carrying several tags to follow kinetochores (Mtw1-mCHERRY), centrosomes (Spc42-CFP) and tubulin (TUB1-GFP)) revealed a large population of non-dividing cells as well as a significant decrease in the number of cells that have started to separate their chromosomes (Figure 2b).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2b.

claims.claim: In some cells transformed with 2µ∆NEG, the whole spindle apparatus was able to traverse to the daughter cell before segregation.
claims.source: Interestingly, in some of these cells we observed that the whole spindle apparatus was able to traverse to the daughter cell before segregation (Figure 2c).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2c.

claims.claim: Live microscopy of cells transformed with 2µ∆NEG confirmed a large population of non-dividing cells and a significant number of cells (18% vs 3% in control) in which the nucleus remained undivided for several hours.
claims.source: This analysis confirmed a large population of non-dividing cells in the strain transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector, consistent with previous observations (Morillo-Huesca et al., 2010), and a significant number of cells (18% vs 3% in the control strain) in which the nucleus remained undivided for several hours (Figure 2d, first panel and source data file for Figure 2d).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by live microscopy data shown in Figure 2d and quantification in the source data file.

claims.claim: A small proportion of cells transformed with 2µ∆NEG (8%) showed nuclear migration to the daughter cell before mitosis.
claims.source: The first one was a small proportion of cells (8%) in which the nucleus migrated to the daughter cell before mitosis (Figure 2d, second panel).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by live microscopy data shown in Figure 2d.

claims.claim: Some cells transformed with 2µ∆NEG (1%) undergo aberrant mitosis in which both nuclei remain trapped in the daughter, generating a binucleated cell.
claims.source: The second phenotype involved a combination of the two phenomena previously described and led on some occasions (1%) to an aberrant mitosis in which both nuclei remain trapped in the daughter, generating a binucleated cell (Figure 2d, third panel).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by live microscopy data shown in Figure 2d.

claims.claim: Aberrant mitosis in which the daughter keeps all the genetic material only takes place in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector and never in cells with an empty vector.
claims.source: These movies confirmed that aberrant mitosis in which the daughter (never observed in the mother) keeps all the genetic material only take place in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by live microscopy data comparing cells with 2µ∆NEG versus empty vector.

claims.claim: Binucleated cells arising from aberrant mitosis can undergo a second cell division in which the two nuclear masses are split between mother and daughter.
claims.source: In one of these events, we were able to follow a second cell division of one of these binucleated cells in which the two nuclear masses were split between the mother and the daughter (Figure 2e).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by live microscopy data shown in Figure 2e.

claims.claim: The rad53-AID degron is functional as indicated by low levels of Rad53 after one hour of treatment with 500 µM NAA.
claims.source: The rad53-AID degron was fully functional as indicated by the low level of Rad53 after one hour of treatment with 500 µM NAA (1-Naphthaleneacetic acid, NAA) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a.

claims.claim: rad53-AID mutant cells are sensitive to histone overexpression.
claims.source: rad53-AID mutant cells were sensitive to histone overexpression and deletion of LSM1 was lethal in these cells in the presence of Auxin (Figure 3—figure supplement 1b and c).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by plate growth assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claims.claim: Deletion of LSM1 is lethal in rad53-AID cells in the presence of Auxin.
claims.source: rad53-AID mutant cells were sensitive to histone overexpression and deletion of LSM1 was lethal in these cells in the presence of Auxin (Figure 3—figure supplement 1b and c).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by plate growth assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1c.

claims.claim: 4 hr of Auxin treatment reduces 90% of cell viability in rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells.
claims.source: Indeed, 4 hr of Auxin treatment was sufficient to reduce 90% of cell viability (Figure 3—figure supplement 1d).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by colony formation assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1d.

claims.claim: The lethality of rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells after Auxin treatment is much higher than that observed in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG.
claims.source: This lethality was much higher than the one observed in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG (Figure 3—figure supplement 1e) indicating that this conditional system was much more toxic for the cell.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by viability assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1e.

claims.claim: Rad53 depletion per se has little or no effect on histone accumulation.
claims.source: Quantification of histone levels indicated that Rad53 depletion per se had little or no effect on histone accumulation but did increase histone levels in an lsm1∆ background (Figure 3b).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by quantification of purified histones shown in Figure 3b.

claims.claim: Rad53 depletion increases histone levels in an lsm1∆ background.
claims.source: Quantification of histone levels indicated that Rad53 depletion per se had little or no effect on histone accumulation but did increase histone levels in an lsm1∆ background (Figure 3b).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by quantification of purified histones shown in Figure 3b.

claims.claim: rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells treated with NAA show a significant increase of canonical histones compared to histone H2A.Z levels.
claims.source: Western blot analysis with these samples confirmed a significant increase of canonical histones compared to the levels of histone H2A.Z, a histone variant that is not regulated by Lsm1 as canonical histones (Figure 3c, Figure 3—figure supplement 3f).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3c and quantification in Figure 3—figure supplement 3f.

claims.claim: rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells display an aberrant nucleosome pattern with chromatin that is less accessible to MNase digestion.
claims.source: rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells displayed a clear aberrant nucleosome pattern. While mono and di-nucleosomes were visible at concentrations ranging from 2.5 to 5 mU of Mnase in controls, chromatin from rad53-AID-lsm1-treated cells produced a high-molecular-weight smear that suggests that this chromatin is somehow less accesible to Mnase digestion.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by MNase digestion data shown in Figure 3d.

claims.claim: High levels of histones are able to promote changes in chromatin structure.
claims.source: Overall, our results indicate that the rad53-AID lsm1∆ system constitutes a good tool to generate conditional large accumulations of histones in the cell and that high levels of histones are able to promote changes in chromatin structure.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by MNase digestion data showing altered chromatin accessibility in Figure 3d.

claims.claim: Live microscopy of rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells reveals a large majority of cells that arrest as large budded cells in which the nucleus migrates between the mother and the daughter cell.
claims.source: We next sought to investigate if this system phenocopied some of the cell cycle defects observed in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector. Live microscopy and DAPI staining analysis of rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells reveals a large majority of cells that arrest as large budded cells in which the nucleus migrates between the mother and the daughter cell (Figure 3e and Figure 3—video 1 and 2)
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by live microscopy data shown in Figure 3e.

claims.claim: rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells usually die after 6–8 hr of NAA treatment and are unable to enter or skip mitosis.
claims.source: These cells usually died after 6–8 hr of NAA treatment and were unable to enter or skip mitosis.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by live microscopy observations.

claims.claim: FACS analysis suggests that most rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells are able to complete replication.
claims.source: FACS analysis suggested that most of them were able to complete replication (Figure 3f).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3f.

claims.claim: rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells treated for 4 hr with NAA exhibit a PFGE pattern similar to cells treated with Nocodazole and different from cells treated with Hydroxyurea.
claims.source: Cells treated for 4 hr with NAA exhibited a similar pattern to the one observed in cells treated with Nocodazole and clearly different from the one observed in cells treated with Hydroxyurea that leads to the accumulation of cells that have not fully replicated their DNA (Figure 3g).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by PFGE data shown in Figure 3g.

claims.claim: Treatment with Auxin specifically raises a population of rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells that had doubled their DNA content.
claims.source: Treatment with Auxin specifically raised a population of cells that had doubled their DNA content (Figure 3h).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by FACS data shown in Figure 3h.

claims.claim: Cse4CENP-A lies at the centromere and is essential to recruit the kinetochore.
claims.source: Cse4CENP-A and Htz1H2A.Z are two histone variants that can replace canonical histones H3 and H2A, respectively. Cse4CENP-A lies at the centromere and is essential to recruit the kinetochore (Stoler et al., 1995; Meluh et al., 1998; Fachinetti et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claims.claim: Htz1H2A.Z is enriched at the centromere and pericentromeric regions and is required for efficient chromosome segregation.
claims.source: Htz1H2A.Z is enriched at the centromere and pericentromeric regions and is required for efficient chromosome segregation (Albert et al., 2007; Krogan et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claims.claim: Cse4CENP-A incorporation outside of the centromere region has been linked to WGDs in certain tumours.
claims.source: Cse4CENP-A incorporation outside of the centromere region has been previously linked to WGDs in certain tumours (Tomonaga et al., 2003) and to aneuploidy in yeast (Castillo et al., 2007; Collins et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claims.claim: High levels of Htz1H2A.Z incorporation at the pericentromeric region in yeast affects ploidy.
claims.source: Similarly, high-levels of Htz1H2A.Z incorporation at the pericentromeric region in yeast also affected ploidy (Chambers et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claims.claim: Histone overexpression is able to promote changes in centromeric chromatin.
claims.source: Since histone overexpression is able to promote changes in centromeric chromatin (Au et al., 2008; Castillo et al., 2007; Salzler et al., 2009; Takayama et al., 2010) we checked if high levels of histones were able to promote WGDs by changing the stoichiometry of canonical histones versus non-canonical histones at centromeric chromatin.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claims.claim: High levels of histones do not change the amount of Cse4CENP-A at centromeres.
claims.source: Analysis of several regions of chromosomes IV and XII revealed no changes in the amount of Cse4CENP-A at centromeres (Figure 4a, left panel).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4a.

claims.claim: Canonical histones increase their occupancy along several regions and are highly enriched at centromeres under high histone conditions.
claims.source: Canonical histones in contrast did increase their occupancy along several regions and were highly enriched at centromeres (Figure 4a, middle and right panels).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4a.

claims.claim: Mtw1 recruitment to centromeres is similar in rad53-AID and rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells and does not significantly increase in other regions of the genome.
claims.source: Mtw1 recruitment to centromeres IV and XII was similar and did not significantly increased in other regions of the genome.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4b and 4c.

claims.claim: Most rad53-AID lsm1∆ arrested cells display one single mass of chromosomes in the daughter or mother cell that remains in line with the spindle axis.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 4d, most of the arrested cells displayed one single mass of chromosomes in the daughter or the mother cell that always remained in line with the spindle axis.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4d.

claims.claim: Histone overexpression does not affect CENP-A recruitment, the attachment of kinetochores to chromosomes, or the attachment of both to the spindle.
claims.source: We concluded that histone overexpression is able to increase histone H3 and H4 occupancy at centromeres and several other regions but this incorporation does not seem to affect CENP-A recruitment, the attachment of kinetochores to chromosomes, or the attachment of both to the spindle.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP-qPCR and microscopy data shown in Figure 4.

claims.claim: There is a clear decrease in the incorporation of Htz1H2A.Z to pericentromeric chromatin in rad53-AID lsm1∆ treated cells.
claims.source: We next analysed the recruitment of Htz1H2A.Z to chromatin (Figure 5a). We observed a clear decrease in the incorporation of Htz1H2A.Z to pericentromeric chromatin in agreement with the global decrease of the H2AZ/H4 ratio shown in Figure 3c.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5a.

claims.claim: The decrease in Htz1H2A.Z incorporation is opposite to what was observed for histones H2B and H2A, indicating that Htz1H2A.Z molecules are being replaced by canonical histone H2A.
claims.source: This decrease was opposite to what was observed for histones H2B and H2A and indicated that Htz1H2A.Z molecules were being replaced by the canonical histone H2A in the rad53-AID lsm1∆ mutant treated with Auxin.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5a.

claims.claim: The level of Htz1H2A.Z is decreased in wild-type cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector.
claims.source: Interestingly, although wild-type cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector do not seem to increase the protein levels of H2B (see above Figure 1f), the level of Htz1H2A.Z was decreased in these cells (Figure 5b and c).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5b and quantification in Figure 5c.

claims.claim: Htz1H2A.Z overexpression largely increases the levels of Htz1H2A.Z in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector.
claims.source: Htz1H2A.Z overexpression using a high copy vector largely increased the levels of Htz1H2A.Z observed in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector (Figure 5d)
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5d.

claims.claim: Htz1H2A.Z overexpression decreases the amount of WGDs observed in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector.
claims.source: Htz1H2A.Z overexpression using a high copy vector largely increased the levels of Htz1H2A.Z observed in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG vector (Figure 5d) and was able to decrease the amount of WGDs observed in these cells (Figure 5e).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by WGD quantification data shown in Figure 5e.

claims.claim: Deletion of SWR1 increases the formation of WGDs in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG.
claims.source: Consistent with the result of Figure 5e, deletion of SWR1, which decreases Htz1H2A.Z incorporation to chromatin (Mizuguchi et al., 2004) had an opposite effect to the one conferred by Htz1H2A.Z overexpression and increased the formation of WGDs in cells transformed with the 2µ∆NEG (Figure 5f).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by time course data shown in Figure 5f.

claims.claim: Overexpression of Htz1H2A.Z in rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells is unable to suppress the defect in the incorporation of this histone variant to chromatin, the G2/M arrest or the lethality after NAA treatment.
claims.source: Overexpression of histone Htz1H2A.Z in rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells also increased the amounts of total histone Htz1H2A.Z (Figure 5—figure supplement 5b) but was unable to supress the defect in the incorporation of this histone variant to chromatin, the G2/M arrest or the lethality after NAA treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1c, d ane e).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1c, d, and e.

claims.claim: Htz1H2A.Z relative levels are important in the generation of WGDs in cells exposed to persistent transcription of histones H2A and H2B.
claims.source: In summary, our results with the 2µ∆NEG vector indicate that Htz1H2A.Z relative levels are important in the generation of WGDs in cells exposed to a persistent transcription of histones H2A and H2B.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by data showing that H2A.Z overexpression reduces WGDs and SWR1 deletion increases WGDs in 2µ∆NEG cells.

claims.claim: Excessive incorporation of Htz1H2A.Z to pericentromeric chromatin has been linked to WGDs.
claims.source: Excessive incorporation of Htz1H2A.Z to pericentromeric chromatin has been previously linked to WGDs (Chambers et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claims.claim: In S. pombe, Htz1H2A.Z is required to stabilize the recruitment of condensin to pericentromeres.
claims.source: In S. pombe Htz1H2A.Z is required to stabilise the recruitment of condensin to pericentromeres, a complex able to embrace each of the daughter DNA strands and required to allow their proper segregation (Cuylen and Haering, 2011; Kim et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claims.claim: Depletion of the CAP-H kleisin subunit (Brn1) of Condensin II in drosophila S2 cells leads to chromosome segregation defects and produces a small number of abortive mitosis in which all genetic material is retained in one cell.
claims.source: Depletion of the CAP-H kleisin subunit (Brn1) of Condensin II in drosophila S2 cells has been shown to lead to chromosome segregation defects and produce a small number of abortive mitosis in which all the genetic material is retained in one cell (Oliveira et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claims.claim: Mutations in the condensin II subunit Caph2 in mice have been involved in the generation of cells with increased ploidy content.
claims.source: Mutations in the condensin II subunit Caph2 in mice have also been recently involved in the generation of cells with an increased ploidy content (Woodward et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claims.claim: Recruitment of Brn1 to pericentromeric chromatin decreases in three out of four pericentromeres examined in rad53-AID lsm1∆ treated cells.
claims.source: Recruitment of Brn1 to pericentromeric chromatin decreased in three out of the four pericentromeres examined in five independent experiments suggesting that Htz1H2A.Z is important for condensin recruitment to pericentromeric regions in S. cerevisiae.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 5g.

claims.claim: Htz1H2A.Z is important for condensin recruitment to pericentromeric regions in S. cerevisiae.
claims.source: Recruitment of Brn1 to pericentromeric chromatin decreased in three out of the four pericentromeres examined in five independent experiments suggesting that Htz1H2A.Z is important for condensin recruitment to pericentromeric regions in S. cerevisiae.
claims.evidence: This statement is inferred from the observation that decreased H2A.Z incorporation correlates with decreased Brn1 recruitment.

claims.claim: The smc2-8 mutant is extremely sensitive to histone overexpression.
claims.source: The smc2-8 mutant, was extremely sensitive to histone overexpression (Figure 5h) further linking histone levels to condensin function.
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by plate growth assay data shown in Figure 5h.

claims.claim: Auxin treatment in rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells does not promote Pds1Securin phosphorylation.
claims.source: Auxin treatment in rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells did not promote Pds1Securin phosphorylation (Figure 6a), a marker for DDR activation
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6a.

claims.claim: Auxin treatment in rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells does not enhance the formation of Mad2 foci at kinetochores.
claims.source: Auxin treatment in rad53-AID lsm1∆ cells did not promote Pds1Securin phosphorylation (Figure 6a), a marker for DDR activation, or enhanced the formation of Mad2 foci at kinetochores, a marker used to detect SAC activation (Figure 6b).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6b.

claims.claim: rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells show a slight stabilization of Pds1SECURIN during G2/M release.
claims.source: This experiment revealed a slight stabilisation of Pds1SECURIN in rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells, higher levels of Scc1Rad21, the main substrate of Pds1, and Clb2 (Figure 6c and Figure 6—figure supplement 1a and b).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6c.

claims.claim: Clb2 starts to degrade but reaccumulates later in rad53-AID-lsm1∆-treated cells, suggesting that APC-Cdh1 activity is impaired.
claims.source: Clb2 started to degrade but reaccumulated later suggesting that the activity of APC-Cdh1 is impaired in this mutant.
claims.evidence: This statement is inferred from the observation of Clb2 protein levels during the time course.

claims.claim: Swe1WEE1 is stabilized in a hypophosphorylated form in rad53-lsm1∆-treated cells.
claims.source: We next looked at Swe1WEE1 levels and observed that this kinase was stabilised in a hypophosphorylated form in rad53-lsm1∆-treated cells (Figure 6d).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6d.

claims.claim: Swe1WEE1 stabilization leads to higher levels of Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation that depend on Swe1WEE1.
claims.source: This stabilisation led to a higher level of Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation that depend on Swe1WEE1 (Figure 6e)
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6e.

claims.claim: Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation in rad53-lsm1∆-treated cells is independent of the DDR, since MEC1 deletion does not abolish it.
claims.source: This stabilisation led to a higher level of Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation that depend on Swe1WEE1 (Figure 6e) and was independent of the DDR, since MEC1 deletion did not abolish it (Figure 6f).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6f.

claims.claim: SWE1 deletion suppresses Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation but is unable to suppress Pds1 stabilization.
claims.source: SWE1 deletion was able to suppress Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation but unable to suppress Pds1 stabilisation suggesting that the mechanism by which Pds1 is stabilised does not depend on Cdc28CDK1 activity (Figure 6g and Figure 6—figure supplement 1c).
claims.evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6g.

results.result: Abnormal accumulations of histones are sufficient to induce whole-genome duplications (WGDs) in S. cerevisiae. This was demonstrated using both centromeric and high-copy vectors expressing histones H2A/H2B beyond S-phase (ΔNEG constructs) in rad53K227A, tom1Δ, and wild-type backgrounds, with WGD frequencies ranging from 1-4×10⁻². The resulting diploids were viable, showed no major chromosome reorganization, and could form triploids when crossed.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C20-C31 provide converging evidence from multiple experimental systems (CEN-ΔNEG in mutants, 2μ-ΔNEG in wild-type) showing that histone overexpression induces WGDs. FACS analysis, karyotyping, growth assays, and control experiments with empty vectors support the conclusion. The frequency quantification and characterization of diploid properties strengthen the result.

results.result: Histone overexpression causes cell cycle defects including delayed chromosome segregation and aberrant cell divisions where daughter cells retain all genetic material. Live microscopy revealed that 18% of 2μΔNEG cells maintain undivided nuclei for hours, 8% show nuclear migration to daughters before mitosis, and 1% undergo aberrant mitosis producing binucleated daughter cells that can subsequently divide to generate diploids.
results.evaluation: Claims C32-C39 describe the cellular mechanism underlying WGD formation using time-course FACS, fixed-cell microscopy, and live-cell imaging. The quantification of specific phenotypes (18%, 8%, 1%) and observation of binucleated cells undergoing subsequent division provide mechanistic insight into how WGDs arise. Controls with empty vectors confirm specificity.

results.result: The rad53-AID lsm1Δ system provides a conditional tool to generate large accumulations of histones. Auxin treatment depletes Rad53 and combined with lsm1Δ increases histone levels, alters the canonical histone/H2A.Z ratio, and produces aberrant chromatin structure with reduced MNase accessibility. This system is highly toxic (90% lethality at 4h) and phenocopies defects observed with constitutive histone overexpression.
results.evaluation: Claims C40-C49 establish and validate the rad53-AID lsm1Δ system through Western blots showing Rad53 depletion, histone quantification, chromatin analysis, and viability assays. The MNase digestion data demonstrating altered chromatin structure provides direct evidence that high histone levels affect chromatin organization. Multiple controls (single mutants, untreated cells) support the conclusions.

results.result: rad53-AID lsm1Δ cells treated with auxin arrest as large-budded cells with nuclei migrating between mother and daughter, complete DNA replication (confirmed by FACS and PFGE), but die after 6-8h without entering mitosis. A subset of surviving cells experience WGDs.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C54 characterize the cell cycle phenotype of the rad53-AID lsm1Δ system using live microscopy, FACS, and PFGE. The PFGE comparison with nocodazole (replicated) vs hydroxyurea (unreplicated) controls provides strong evidence that cells complete replication before arrest. FACS data showing diploid survivors confirms WGD occurrence.

results.result: High histone levels reduce H2A.Z incorporation to pericentromeric chromatin, and H2A.Z levels are critical for WGD formation. ChIP-qPCR shows decreased H2A.Z at pericentromeric regions in rad53-AID lsm1Δ treated cells and 2μΔNEG cells. H2A.Z overexpression reduces WGDs in 2μΔNEG cells while SWR1 deletion increases WGDs. However, H2A.Z overexpression cannot rescue rad53-AID lsm1Δ defects.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C65-C72 establish the link between histone overexpression, reduced H2A.Z incorporation, and WGDs through ChIP-qPCR, Western blots, and genetic manipulation experiments. The bidirectional genetic evidence (overexpression reduces, deletion increases WGDs) in the 2μΔNEG system is compelling. The inability of H2A.Z overexpression to rescue rad53-AID lsm1Δ suggests additional chromatin structural defects in that system.

results.result: Histone overexpression increases canonical histone occupancy at centromeres and other regions without affecting CENP-A (Cse4) levels, kinetochore attachment (Mtw1 recruitment), or spindle-kinetochore connections. Arrested cells maintain chromosomes aligned along the spindle axis.
results.evaluation: Claims C60-C64 use ChIP-qPCR and microscopy to demonstrate that increased histone occupancy does not disrupt centromere identity or kinetochore function. The data showing maintained Mtw1 recruitment and chromosome alignment along the spindle axis rule out gross defects in chromosome-spindle attachment, helping to narrow the mechanism of WGD formation.

results.result: High histone levels reduce condensin (Brn1) recruitment to pericentromeric chromatin. ChIP-qPCR shows decreased Brn1 at 3 of 4 pericentromeres examined in rad53-AID lsm1Δ treated cells. The condensin mutant smc2-8 is extremely sensitive to histone overexpression, linking histone levels to condensin function.
results.evaluation: Claims C77-C79 connect reduced H2A.Z incorporation to decreased condensin recruitment through ChIP-qPCR data (5 independent experiments) and genetic interaction with smc2-8. The consistency across multiple pericentromeres and the synthetic lethality with condensin mutation provide strong support for this mechanism linking histone overexpression to chromosome segregation defects.

results.result: High histone levels promote Swe1WEE1 stabilization in a hypophosphorylated form, leading to Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation at Tyr19 through a mechanism independent of the canonical DNA damage response. SWE1 deletion suppresses Cdc28 phosphorylation but not Pds1 stabilization, indicating Pds1 stabilization is independent of Cdc28 activity.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C5, C84-C88 demonstrate Swe1 stabilization and Cdc28 phosphorylation through Western blots in rad53-AID lsm1Δ cells. The MEC1 deletion experiment (C86) rules out DDR involvement. The genetic dissection showing SWE1 deletion affects Cdc28 but not Pds1 (C87-C88) provides clear epistasis data supporting independent pathways.

results.result: Cells overexpressing histones do not activate the canonical DNA damage response (no Rad53 phosphorylation or Ddc2 foci) but show slightly increased Mad2 foci suggesting possible SAC activation. Cdc28CDK1 phosphorylation is prolonged in rad53K227A cells overexpressing histones, linking Cdc28 phosphorylation directly to high histone levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C94 characterize checkpoint responses in 2μΔNEG cells through Western blots, microscopy, and cell cycle time courses. The absence of DDR markers combined with modest Mad2 increase and prolonged Cdc28 phosphorylation in rad53K227A background provides evidence for a non-canonical response to histone stress. The rad53K227A experiment (C92-C94) is particularly informative.

results.result: WGDs from histone overexpression are not caused by persistent checkpoint activation. rad53-AID lsm1Δ cells show no Pds1 phosphorylation or enhanced Mad2 foci, only slight Pds1 stabilization. MAD2 and SWE1 deletions accelerate WGDs in 2μΔNEG cells and partially suppress arrest in rad53-AID lsm1Δ when combined, suggesting the SAC and Swe1 cooperate to prevent rather than cause WGDs.
results.evaluation: Claims C80-C83, C95-C100 use checkpoint marker analysis and genetic deletion experiments to demonstrate that checkpoints are not the cause of WGDs. The key evidence is that checkpoint deletions accelerate rather than prevent WGDs (C96), and the double deletion suppresses arrest (C98). This counterintuitive result is well-supported by the data and suggests checkpoints provide a protective response.

results.result: The authors propose a model where high histone levels increase nucleosome occupancy, reduce nucleosome-free regions, decrease H2A.Z incorporation through competition with canonical H2A, impair condensin recruitment, and ultimately cause chromosome segregation defects leading to WGDs. This explains why histone expression is normally restricted to S-phase.
results.evaluation: Claims C101-C103, C106-C109 present the mechanistic model integrating the experimental findings. The model is well-supported by the data showing increased nucleosome occupancy (C61, C106), decreased H2A.Z incorporation (C65-C66), reduced condensin recruitment (C77), and the genetic evidence linking these events to WGDs. The model provides a coherent explanation for the observations.

results.result: The stabilization of Swe1WEE1 under high histone conditions reveals a general role for Swe1 in histone metabolism. Combined with prior work showing Cdc28CDK1 regulation responds to low histone levels, this suggests Cdc28 regulation may be a general mechanism for cells to respond to both high and low histone levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C114 and C116 synthesize the current findings with published literature to propose a broader role for Swe1/Cdc28 in histone homeostasis. The inference is reasonable given the data showing Swe1 stabilization (C84) and Cdc28 phosphorylation (C85) in response to high histones, combined with cited work on low histone responses (C115).

results.result: The authors argue that histone deregulation may be an underappreciated source of genome instability in cancer. They cite evidence linking histone H2A overexpression to hepatocellular carcinoma, SLBP depletion to tetraploidy and tumorigenesis, arsenic-induced SLBP depletion to increased tumorigenicity, and amplification of chromosome 6p (containing histone genes) to cancer aggressiveness.
results.evaluation: Claims C117-C124 are primarily based on citations to published literature and represent the authors' interpretation of the broader significance of their findings. While the cited studies support connections between histone dysregulation and cancer, the claims about histone deregulation being an "important and yet unexplored potential source of genome instability" (C123) are speculative extrapolations from the yeast data. The relevance to human cancer requires additional validation.

results.result: Background claims establishing prior knowledge about histone regulation, cell cycle checkpoints, and Swe1WEE1 function in yeast and higher eukaryotes.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C19 provide established background knowledge supported by appropriate citations to published literature. These claims set the context for the experimental work but do not represent novel findings from this study.

results.result: Background claims about histone variants (CENP-A, H2A.Z), condensin function, checkpoint responses, and prior work on histone overexpression effects, establishing the rationale for investigating H2A.Z and condensin in the context of histone-induced WGDs.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C59, C73-C76, C104-C105, C110-C113, C115 provide relevant background from published literature that motivates the experimental approaches and interpretation. These are appropriately cited and accurately represent prior work, but are not novel findings from this manuscript.
